description: Heading to the scrap yard to find the statue, "Good luck to us and good luck to you." The scrap yard owner reluctantly cooperates.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Pretending to be slightly busy, cautiously bypassing this area, preparing to see if I can smoothly enter the prop room from the side door.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You pass through the chaotic backstage, seeing actors not yet called for rehearsal gathered in small groups—some sobbing softly, others suddenly bursting into song, emotions swinging violently between sorrow and excitement. Portraits of Caterina are everywhere; in those photos adorned with rose wreaths, her gaze seems to truly follow everyone who passes by.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Oh no, my skepticism is rising again. The fragment wouldn't be on that person. This strange ability to influence. No matter how high the looks, it shouldn't be like this.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: #First, take a medium-sized object in the prop room to carry, so as not to arouse suspicion.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Just as Bailan tries to slip quietly toward the side door, she suddenly hears a strange clattering sound—turning to see a row of plaster arms, legs, and heads strung together with hemp rope being dragged down the corridor. Those pale limbs collide with each other, emitting a teeth-grating friction sound. Before she can react, a chariot wheel studded with fake gems suddenly detaches and rolls toward you at an unnaturally fast speed. You scramble to dodge, forced into that passageway. In the dim passage, the surroundings become increasingly bizarre—several actors playing Egyptian soldiers stagger past, the fake blood on their costumes looking as fresh as if just splashed on. These actors wear exaggerated smiles, loudly singing a triumphant march, their prop spears trembling and constantly striking the ground. Suddenly, a rumbling sound comes from deep within the corridor—dozens of wooden severed heads roll like bowling balls, their hollow eye sockets glowing eerily under the kerosene lamps. You are forced to retreat into a darker side passage, backs pressed against the cold walls.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The investigators are completely lost in the labyrinthine backstage corridors. Their hushed pleas for help are swallowed entirely by the darkness; the corridor walls seem to slowly contract and expand, as if breathing. At a certain corner, a group of chorus members in costumes suddenly appears, walking backward, wearing Egyptian god masks with the backs facing forward. When the investigators try to approach and ask for directions, these people dissipate like smoke around the corner. Something whispers in the darkness; listening carefully, it's lines from Aida. The room nameplates on both sides of the corridor flicker before your eyes, changing to different room names with each blink. The sense of time is completely disrupted—Toscanini's roars sound both distant and close at hand, as if happening simultaneously in the past and future.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Frowning, taking out a marker pen, leaving marks on the nearby wall to ensure I don't walk the same path repeatedly.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Most terrifyingly, they begin to find this madness perfectly reasonable. player4 finds himself nodding along to a non-existent rhythm; Bailan finds the marks her marker pen leaves on the wall are the cursed patterns from her left arm. Here, the laws of reality have been altered; they have entered a world full of tricks and deception and are becoming engrossed in it. They are backstage, fallen into a party hosted by the artistic clockwork demon.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: #Using the crowbar to forcefully strike the ground, listening for echoes to ensure we haven't been transported to an empty area.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Knocking player4's head "Stop nodding, act normal."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Trying to snap out of it.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: When the third group of slave actors wearing metal shackles leaps past the corridor with eerie laughter, the investigators feel a strong wave of dizziness—the clanging sounds of those shackles are like a hypnotic pendulum, making one involuntarily want to give up all investigation.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bailan suddenly feels the statues in the prop room are not important at all; these frenzied performances before her eyes are the true reality of the world. Her fingers trace the peeling paint on the wall, finding it more beautiful than any archaeological discovery.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Eh... Another sanity check? I understand, everyone's watching.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Johnson stood in the center of the corridor laughing heartily, believing the entire kidnapping was a brilliant piece of improvisational theater. As the slave actors danced around him, he almost joined their ranks.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Kick Johnson hard

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Eh... Another sanity check? I understand, everyone's watching.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The backstage had now become a vortex of dreams and madness, every prop whispering to give up.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Tap the props, look for sound devices

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player2 has not heard the whispers of the props.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "What's wrong with you all?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Some not particularly interesting segments."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #At this point, a purely Muggle decision: check out the prop room.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Pushing open the door, you're hit by the heavy smell of fabric, paint, and tobacco mixed together. The cramped prop room is as crowded as a Pullman carriage, with fabric rolls, spools, and design sketches piled against all four walls.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Hello, ma'am."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hello, ma'am."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: (Barbecue

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Louisa looks up from her design, ash falling onto the gold dust: Non-staff are not allowed. She squints her smoke-yellowed eyes, what are you here for?

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Apologies for disturbing your work at this time, but we have a more urgent matter concerning the case of the lead actress of this grand opera, our dear star lady."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We are detectives hired by Ms. Caterina's agent to investigate her disappearance. We've traced some clues to the prop room, that's why we're here."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Translate blah blah blah

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "This is the pass specially approved for us by Mr. Rossi, please take a look."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "There seem to be some hidden clues in this prop room, a white statue. I wonder if you've seen it, ma'am."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Louisa takes the pass, glances at it casually, and continues revising her design: Detectives? That fool Rossi finally willing to spend money? She points her pen tip towards six plaster statues in the corner: The newly purchased mannequins are all over there, take a look yourselves.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Thank you, ma'am."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: One of the elderly women in black suddenly speaks simultaneously. player2 can understand: The seventh one was too big—it was moved somewhere downstairs. Louisa translates without looking up: They say the seventh old mannequin was recently moved downstairs.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Alright, thank you."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I think we'd better not separate."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Ok"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Briefly inspect the 6 statues.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Oh"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Professor Bailan approaches the six plaster mannequins and carefully examines their material. These new statues are made of ordinary plaster, with smooth polished surfaces and metal bolts at the joints, completely standard tailor's dummies.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Gently tap to determine if it's solid or hollow inside

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Solid.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Recall

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The furnishings here are exactly the same as in the dream.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Search for the cabinet containing the statue according to memory

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Then, shouldn't we go downstairs to look?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Dear lady, has anyone taken the things that were previously inside this cabinet?"

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Indeed, let's go downstairs and take a look." #Preparing to act.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Louisa stretched her neck to glance, ash falling on the design draft: Ah, the old mannequin used to stand right there. She pointed her pencil at the floor. Last month, during the rehearsal of the second act of Aida, Toscanini had a sudden idea and insisted on moving it downstairs to serve as Radamès' armor stand.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Run, run!

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: I suggest you go during the day—since that thing was moved downstairs, four night-shift prop masters have already quit. That statue was unsettling even when it was up here. By the way, let me tell you, of the over twenty employees who have resigned in the past six years, thirteen were involved in Aida prop maintenance. Louisa said, looking down, gold dust slipping through her fingers. The reason I'm fine is probably because I only handle costume design.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Since things have come to this, player2 goes downstairs and sees the stone statue. Now that he has seen it, he observes it.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "That really is a troublesome matter."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Pushing open the heavy fire door reveals a brightly lit rehearsal hall. Toscanini stands with his back to the door, angrily tapping the music stand with his baton: Aida's lament should sound like a cry for help drowned by the Nile! Not your constipated moaning! The actors nervously repeat their lines, sweat soaking their costumes.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Nothing, what now?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Points at himself "Me, go negotiate with this kind of lunatic, really?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hey, I have a good idea."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: What are you rats muttering about?! "Toscanini suddenly turns around, bloodshot eyes fixed directly on you.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: #Shields the group, "Alright, alright, calm down."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Sir, please calm down first! We are detectives investigating the disappearance of Ms. Caterina. We can help you resolve your current predicament!"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Toscanini's face instantly turns beet red: Detectives?! He sputters, my prima donna is missing, and you useless lot are sniffing around backstage like dogs in heat!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Building on the companion's words, trying hard to convince him we are here to help.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: He grabs a timpani mallet and hurls it at the wall: Do you know what time it is?! There are only—he yanks his bowtie loose—thirty-seven hours until the premiere! And you are disturbing the only person who can make these tone-deaf fools sound less like braying donkeys!

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Thinking whether to retort or how to proceed?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "This is the place Ms. Caterina frequented most. Our being here is perfectly reasonable!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "But, just as only pigs can find truffles, you have to let the pigs try, don't you?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Who let you in?! Toscanini grabs player4's tie, yanking him off balance. My theater is not a damned tourist attraction! He roars towards the second floor, Guards! Throw these trespassing vermin out!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "And there are clues pointing here."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Observe if the maestro has something on him.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Whisper in his ear.

conversation.speaker: player1

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Toscanini takes a deep breath, barely suppressing his anger, and asks in a slightly calmer tone: Alright, what exactly do you want? What are you searching for? What are you looking at?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Last month, did you move a statue down from upstairs?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "The one that was originally placed in the cabinet."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Toscanini's frown deepens: That old model? Yes, I had it moved backstage. I thought it was more suitable as a armor stand for Radamès. He eyes player4 suspiciously, What? Does a broken statue have something to do with Caterina's disappearance?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We have reason to believe this matter is related to Miss Caterina."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: His fingers unconsciously rub his neck, where the skin seems somewhat red.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Narrow eyes to carefully observe that area

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Stealthily stand to the side of a companion, quietly observing the neck

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Simultaneously continue speaking

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "It's mainly related to the group that kidnapped her."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "That's no ordinary statue; several forces have come for it."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You carefully observe Toscanini's neck and find it's just a common rash, possibly caused by anger or collar friction. No curse markings, no abnormal swelling—just the kind of skin condition any long-term sleep-deprived, irritable artist might have.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We cannot disclose more information. Is the reason sufficient now, sir?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Toscanini frowns deeply: You'll have to ask Marco for the specifics—He turns and shouts towards the backstage, Marco! Come here!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Who handled this matter?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Toscanini's face instantly turns purplish-red: You idiot! He grabs Marco by the collar, spittle flying, That was the armor stand for Radamès I personally designated! A key prop for the second act of Aida!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Watch the show

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Marco's legs tremble with fear: B-but, Maestro... the warehouse records show you signed the disposal form.... And it was so old, the joints were loose... Toscanini angrily throws the sheet music on the ground: What I signed was for a 1872 Scala Opera House antique! Go find it back immediately!

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Was it sold or how was it disposed of?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Observe his expression

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "At least, your reason is needed."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: He turns to the investigators, saying through gritted teeth: It seems you'll have to try your luck at the scrapyard or the collector's place—if that thing hasn't already been chopped into firewood!
